transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-14
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Leo Park (Redwood SE), Jared Bloom (Terrafold), Priya Nair (Terrafold), Samir Patel (Terrafold)

Summary (auto): quick console tour focused on per-route telemetry, cost decomposition, and pilot scoping. Security questions around VPC/KMS and SOC2. Agreed to pilot two high-volume routes; Redwood to send pilot docs + cost export.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving time. Quick intros — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, Leo's our SE who will run the demo.
[00:18] Jared: Hey, Jared here — Head of ML at Terrafold. We're looking to get better visibility on inference spend across our pipelines.
[00:25] Priya: Priya, platform eng — I'll own the pilot infra bits.
[00:30] Samir: Samir, eng mgr — interested on SLOs and rollout.
[00:35] Leo: Great, I'll share my screen. Quick note — we'll walk the Console usage analytics, then route dashboards, and show cost breakdowns per route, including token-level and model variant splits.
[01:05] Leo: (screen) So this is the Redwood Console home, quick nav — usage lens, route explorer, and cost attribution. You might see some names differ, the transcript sometimes spells it Redwood "Consul" or "Consolee" — ignore typos.
[01:30] Priya: Cool, can you surface how you tie requests back to our routes? We run a tagging layer in front of the model endpoints.
[01:40] Leo: Yeah, we ingest route metadata from the request header — route_id, team, and feature flag. In the Console, route explorer shows throughput, p95 latency, and token volume. Here's an example route heatmap.
[02:15] Leo: Notice the per-route cost column — this uses our Compute + Token math, plus any dedup/cache savings from prefix caching. You can filter by model or by region.
[02:45] Jared: When you say caching savings, is that KV cache? We use a custom cache layer internally, curious if Redwood's prefix cache will conflict.
[02:55] Leo: Good question. Our cache is prefix/KV-aware and can be toggled per-route; it doesn't override your app-level cache. If you have an external cache, we recommend turning off automatic prefix caching for that route.
[03:20] Samir: Walk me through the cost breakdown for a single route — what granularity do we get?
[03:30] Leo: Per-route, you get token split (prompt vs completion), model variant cost, GPU compute time estimates, and any quantization/adaptive batching savings. Here's the cost waterfall view.
[03:50] [03:50] (brief pause while switching tabs)
[04:10] Leo: Example: Route "ingest-nlp" — shows 1.2M tokens this month, 70% prompt, 30% completion, model mix: 60% gpt‑j-quant, 40% gpt-3-compat. The Console computes unit costs based on your pricing profile.
[04:40] Priya: How accurate are those compute time estimates? We need to map to our internal chargeback.
[04:50] Leo: Estimates are driven by telemetry we collect — per-token latency histograms and model perf profiles. For dedicated/private customers you can get even tighter numbers by running a short perf probe we provide.
[05:20] Jared: Ok, so for pilot we'd like exact per-route spend to compare with our existing GA bill.
[05:30] Maya: We'll export the per-route CSV (route_id, tokens, model, estimated GPU-seconds, cost) as part of the pilot deliverables.
[05:40] Priya: Must include tags so our billing system can ingest.
[05:45] Leo: Yep — the export includes tags and timestamps.
[06:05] Jared: Security — SOC2, encryption, KMS — what's standard? We'll need SOC2 Type II and KMS integration.
[06:15] Maya: We're SOC2 certified; I'll attach the SOC2 pack. For customer-managed keys, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations and for hosted we offer envelope encryption + bring-your-own-key in the VPC model.
[06:35] Priya: If we do a pilot in your hosted environment, can we restrict logs retention? We have retention policies.
[06:45] Leo: Yes, you can configure retention per-workspace; logs can be redacted and retention shortened. We'll share the exact controls in the security doc.
[07:10] Samir: Regarding latency — our SLAs are tight (p50 < 40ms for short prompts). How do you balance batching vs latency?
[07:20] Leo: Console Optimize module recommends batching thresholds. For latency-sensitive routes we set batch size = 1 or use instant lanes. For high-volume non-latency routes we use async batching. You get route-level SLOs and automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants if a node is saturated.
[07:55] Jared: Any notes on model variants? We run a trimmed smaller model for some endpoints.
[08:05] Leo: Yes — the route explorer shows model mix and supports canary rollouts — you can pin a route to a set of model variants and percentages.
[08:25] [08:25] (someone coughs)
[08:40] Leo: Switching to Alerts and Anomalies — Console flags sudden cost spikes per route and can auto-open a ticket. Here's a sample from another customer where a bad regex generated huge token volume.
[09:05] Priya: Nice. Can we set budget alerts per-team?
[09:10] Maya: Yep — budgets, quota enforcement, and rate limits per-route/team.
[09:22] Jared: What's the onboarding effort for VPC/private? We might want to later go private for PII workloads.
[09:30] Maya: For Private we provide a control plane model — usually 2-4 weeks for initial setup with a standard network runbook. We'll share our private deployment checklist.
[09:45] Samir: Does the pilot require private deployment?
[09:50] Priya: Prefer hosted first, then lift to private if pilot proves out. Lower friction.
[09:55] Leo: That's common — hosted pilot then dedicated pool or private later.
[10:12] Leo: Now I'll drill into the route detail page — you can see token distribution over time with a brush selector, latency percentiles, and an estimated cost per window.
[10:40] Leo: There's also per-route suggestions from Redwood Optimize — e.g., quantize to int8 for this route, or switch to a cheaper variant for < user-visible degradation. The suggestion includes estimated monthly savings.
[11:10] Jared: Can the Optimize suggestions be auto-applied?
[11:18] Leo: They can be staged as proposals; we recommend manual review first, but for mature teams you can enable auto-apply with a rollback window.
[11:40] Priya: For billing mapping, will the cost CSV include currency and full cost breakdown?
[11:47] Leo: Yes — currency, unit costs, compute & token slices, and a breakdown of any discounted reserved capacity if you have Dedicated.
[12:05] Jared: Any gotchas we should know about when matching against our internal billing?
[12:12] Maya: Two common things: tokenization differences (subword/token counts differ slightly across tokenizers) and reserved capacity discounts which reduce per-token within Dedicated. We'll document difference assumptions.
[12:35] Samir: Ok pilot scope — we propose two routes: "query-extract" (latency-sensitive) and "batch-annotate" (throughput-heavy). Can you simulate economics for both?
[12:50] Leo: Absolutely — we'll run a quick cost projection using last month's volumes. I'll produce a small spreadsheet.
[13:05] Priya: We'll need VPC peering contact — who handles that?
[13:10] Maya: I'll include our infra ops contact in the follow-up email.
[13:30] Jared: Timeline — want to be decision-ready in 3 weeks, pilot live in 2-3 weeks after that.
[13:38] Maya: That syncs — our pilot timeline typically 2-4 weeks.
[13:50] Leo: Quick demo note — sometimes transcriptions show model names wrong, like "gpt-j" vs "gpt jv" — but the Console shows exact model slugs in the UI.
[14:05] (screen) Now I'm exporting a per-route CSV for a demo tenant — here's columns: route_id, route_name, team, tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, model_slug, est_gpu_seconds, est_cost_usd.
[14:40] Jared: Perfect, that will map to our cost engine.
[14:50] Priya: Regarding RBAC — can we restrict dashboard views per-team?
[14:56] Leo: Yes, workspace roles + route-level permissions. You can lock down sensitive routes to a limited set of users.
[15:20] Samir: Are audit logs available?
[15:25] Maya: Yes — full audit logs for actions and changes; available via the Console or streamed to your syslog/S3.
[15:50] Jared: Any customers doing chargeback per-feature?
[15:55] Leo: Multiple customers do that; Console supports tagging and chargeback rules. We can demo a sample chargeback rule.
[16:20] Priya: About data residency — we have EU-only PII. Can we restrict route processing to eu-west region?
[16:28] Leo: Absolutely — route-level region pinning is supported; you can pin routes to a region to meet residency needs.
[16:50] (short pause)
[17:05] Maya: Recap — we will: 1) send SOC2 + security pack, 2) Leo to produce per-route CSV and cost projection, 3) schedule a pilot kickoff. Any other asks?
[17:20] Jared: Please include breakdown of expected latency impact if we apply suggested quantization.
[17:25] Leo: Will include that.
[17:40] Priya: Also include the VPC runbook and who's on infra ops.
[17:45] Maya: Noted.
[18:00] Samir: Thanks everyone.
[18:05] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up by EOD with docs and target dates.
[18:15] (meeting ends)

References mentioned: SOC2 pack (link shared in follow-up), pilot template (link), per-route CSV sample (attached by Leo).

Notes on transcription: Minor name and product misspellings, occasional overlapping talk. Action items captured above.
